final:
`public/models/helmet.glb` now uses about 27 MiB of GPU memory, down from 107 MiB. I checked fidelity at 2048px, and it scores 0.933 against the original. The tool treats 0.9 or higher as no visible quality loss.

- **What changed:** the five 2048×2048 textures are now KTX2 (UASC) with quantized geometry. The mesh is unchanged at 15,452 triangles. Babylon.js decodes KTX2 itself, so the scene needs no extra code.
- **Why 2048px:** a first tune at 1024px got GPU memory down to about 7 MiB. That version only holds up when the helmet is viewed at 1024px. At 2048px the same settings dropped to roughly 0.75 fidelity, and VR means close-up viewing. At 2048px, no smaller setting stayed above the 0.9 limit.
- **Trade-off:** the file grew from 3.8 MB to 14.7 MB. That is because the textures stay at full resolution. Download time over 4G goes from about 3.6 s to about 14 s.
- **If memory is still tight:** the 1024px version costs about 7 MiB and 3.3 MB. It will look softer when the helmet is close to the viewer. I can swap it in if you tell me how close users get. The recipe for 2048px is in `recipes/`.
bash_cmds: node-assets tune assets/helmet.glb --for gpu -o recipes/ 2>&1 | tail -50
node-assets tune assets/helmet.glb --for gpu --view 2048 -o recipes/ 2>&1 | tail -30

node-assets run recipes/helmet.gpu.recipe.toon assets/helmet.glb -o public/models/helmet.glb --force 2>&1 | tail -15; node-assets inspect public/models/helmet.glb --against assets/helmet.glb --view 2048 2>&1 | tail -15
